notes.meaning: David looks at the wicked and understands what drives their evil actions. At the root of all their bad choices is a total lack of reverence or respect for God. Because they do not fear the Lord, they feel completely free to live in sin.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early writers like Augustine read this verse as the wicked man telling himself in his own heart that he will sin, deliberately refusing to understand God.

notes.meaning: Wicked people flatter themselves into thinking their sins are small or will never be noticed. They make excuses for their bad behavior instead of being honest about it. In the end, they only despise their wrongdoing when it is uncovered and punished.

The evil inside a person quickly spills out in deceitful and hurtful speech. Such a person may have once done good or known what was right, but he has turned his back on wisdom. He has completely abandoned the path of pleasing God.

Instead of resting or thinking about God at night, the wicked person spends his quiet hours planning evil. He deliberately chooses a harmful way to live and stubbornly sticks to it. He has lost all hatred of wrongdoing and even finds pleasure in doing harm.

David turns his eyes away from human wickedness to the limitless goodness of God. The Lord's loyal love and faithfulness are so vast that they reach higher than the skies and clouds. No human failure can ever exhaust or limit God's promises.

God's righteousness stands firm and unshakeable like the highest mountains. His judgments and purposes run deeper than the ocean, far beyond what human minds can fully grasp. Yet his gentle care reaches every part of creation, watching over both people and animals.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine saw the high mountains as the apostles who received Christ's light first, while the great deep represented the dark abyss of sin into which the wicked sink.

notes.meaning: God's loyal love is a priceless treasure offered to all people. Like young birds finding shelter under a mother's wings, human beings can run to him for safety and comfort. Everyone who trusts in his mercy finds real protection from harm.

Those who take shelter in God receive far more than safety; they are welcomed into a rich feast. God generously satisfies his people through fellowship with him and the blessings of his presence. His spiritual joy flows freely like an endless river.

God is the living spring who gives and sustains all life, both physical and spiritual. His truth shines like bright daylight into a dark world. Only by looking at life through his truth can we clearly understand reality and find genuine joy.

David asks the Lord to keep pouring out his faithful love on those who truly know and honor him. Those who live with an honest heart depend on God's righteousness every single day. His mercy never runs dry for those who trust him.

David prays for protection against arrogant enemies who want to trample him down. He asks God not to let violent hands drive him into exile or push him away from worshipping the Lord. Believers can confidently ask God to shield them from proud oppressors.

Looking ahead with confident faith, David points to the final defeat of the wicked as if it has already happened. Those who build their lives on pride and harm will be cast down and unable to rise again. God's justice guarantees that evil will never have the last word.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writers like Augustine and Jerome understood the word 'there' as referring to pride, viewing pride as the downfall of evil angels and the place where sinners perish.
